## کرش‌هایی که از گزارش خود کاربران پیدا شد

سامانهٔ گزارش کرش کار کرد: ۸۸ خوشه رسید و **۷۴ تای آن‌ها یک باگ واحد بودند.**

### کرش صفحهٔ V2Ray — ۷۴ کاربر
تست پینگ و دیلی و سرعت، نتیجه را بر اساس **جایگاه** در فهرست می‌نوشت:

```kotlin
currentList[index] = updatedNode     // index از عکسِ لحظه‌ای قبل از شروع تست
```

تست دقیقه‌ها طول می‌کشد و فهرست در همان مدت تکان می‌خورد — ایمپورت کانفیگ رایگان، رفرش لینک ساب، حذف یک نود. دو پیامد، بسته به اینکه فهرست بلندتر شده باشد یا کوتاه‌تر:

| نشانه | تعداد |
|---|---|
| نتیجه روی ردیف اشتباه نشست → دو ردیف با یک شناسه → کرش موقع اسکرول | **۶۵ کاربر** |
| ایندکس از انتهای فهرست بیرون زد → `IndexOutOfBoundsException` | **۹ کاربر** |

breadcrumbs دقیقاً سناریو را داد:

```
15:15:08  openTab home -> freeconfig
15:15:12  switchTab freeconfig -> nodes
IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 809 out of bounds for length 8
  at java.util.ArrayList.set
```

حالا همه‌جا بر اساس **شناسه** نوشته می‌شود — نه به ترتیب فهرست کار دارد و نه می‌تواند تکراری بسازد.

### و ترمیم فهرست‌هایی که از قبل خراب شده‌اند
بعد از آن نوشتنِ خراب، فهرست روی دیسک ذخیره می‌شد. یعنی این کاربران **در هر بار باز کردن برنامه دوباره کرش می‌کردند، حتی با کد درست.** فهرست حالا موقع خواندن از شناسه‌های تکراری پاک می‌شود و ذخیرهٔ بعدی نسخهٔ سالم را می‌نویسد.

### «زیردامنه ندارید» به‌عنوان علتِ ناشناخته گزارش می‌شد — ۷ کاربر
کلادفلر می‌گوید «شما زیردامنهٔ workers.dev ندارید» با کد **۱۰۰۰۷** و وضعیت **۴۰۴**. ولی منطق عیب‌یابی فقط حالت ۲۰۰ را برای این وضعیت می‌شناخت، پس به آخرین شاخه می‌افتاد: «علت را نمی‌شناسم، گزارش بفرستید».

یعنی دقیقاً همان کسانی که این صفحه برایشان ساخته شده بود، به‌جای دکمهٔ «ساخت زیردامنه» از آن‌ها گزارش خواسته می‌شد — و جواب داخل همان کدی بود که می‌فرستادند.

### تصویر زمینهٔ بزرگ، دو کرش متفاوت روی دو دستگاه
عکس سفارشی فقط وقتی کوچک می‌شد که اندازهٔ درخواستی معلوم باشد، ولی در **اولین فریم** هنوز صفر است. پس یک عکس هشت‌هزار پیکسلی کامل باز و کش می‌شد:

- روی یک گوشی کانوس از کشیدنش سر باز زد: `Canvas: trying to draw too large (262440000bytes) bitmap`
- روی گوشی دیگری همان تصویر تقریباً کل هیپ ۲۵۶ مگابایتی را گرفت و برنامه سر یک تخصیص **۱۶ بایتی** در صفحهٔ تنظیمات از حافظه کم آورد

سقف اندازه حالا مستقل از درخواست اعمال می‌شود.

### روی اندروید ۷ اولین اتصال برنامه را می‌بست
کانال نوتیفیکیشن از اندروید ۸ به بعد وجود دارد و کمینهٔ پشتیبانی این برنامه اندروید ۷ است. `try/catch` دورش هم کمکی نمی‌کرد، چون `NoSuchMethodError` یک **Error** است نه Exception و از آن رد می‌شود.

### کرش هنگام باز کردن وایرگارد پس از بسته شدن سرویس
اندروید می‌تواند یک درخواست شروع را به سرویسی برساند که در حال از بین رفتن است. کار به یک executor خاموش‌شده سپرده می‌شد و استثنای رد شدنِ کار برنامه را می‌بست. حالا کنار گذاشته و در لاگ ثبت می‌شود.

### باگ خود اندروید ۸ که برنامه را می‌بست
جست‌وجوی کشور نودها از `HttpURLConnection` استفاده می‌کرد که پشتش نسخهٔ داخلی خود اندروید از OkHttp است، و آن نسخه در اندروید ۸٫۰ یک رقابت در استخر اتصال دارد. این روی نخی می‌افتد که برنامه مالکش نیست و **حتی یک فریم از کد ما در استکش نیست**، پس هیچ‌جا نمی‌شد گرفتش. برنامه از قبل OkHttp خودش را دارد که این باگ را ندارد.

releases.title: v1.2.3 — شبکه محلی
releases.notes:
## شبکه محلی — اینترنت گوشی را به دستگاه دیگری بدهید

این نسخه یک قابلیت تازه دارد: **شبکه محلی**. آیکونی تازه در صفحهٔ اصلی که اینترنت تونل‌شدهٔ گوشی را — با سیم یا بی‌سیم، از هر موتوری که روشن باشد — به لپ‌تاپ، تلویزیون یا کنسول می‌دهد، بدون اینکه کسی چیزی از پروکسی بداند.

پیش‌تر این قابلیت یک سوییچ در تنظیمات به نام «اجازه اتصال شبکه محلی» بود و همان سوییچ تمام رابط کاربری‌اش: نه آدرسی که روی دستگاه مقابل وارد کنید، نه راهی برای فهمیدن اینکه کسی وصل شده یا نه، و مهم‌تر از همه هیچ نشانه‌ای از اینکه موتوری که در حال اجراست شاید اصلاً پروکسی منتشر نکند — که در آن حالت سوییچ روشن بود و هیچ اتفاقی نمی‌افتاد.

---

### تازه‌ها

**کافی است یک کد QR را بخوانید — هیچ عددی تایپ نمی‌شود**
تنظیم دستی پروکسی یعنی سه مقدار — آدرس، پورت و نوع — را از صفحهٔ گوشی به دستگاه دیگری منتقل کنید، آن هم از داخل پنجره‌ای که احتمالاً تا حالا بازش نکرده‌اید. پس خود گوشی راهنما را سرو می‌کند: دستگاه مقابل یک QR می‌خواند یا یک لینک باز می‌کند و صفحه‌ای می‌گیرد که خودش تشخیص داده ویندوز است یا مک یا آیفون یا اندروید، و فقط مراحل همان را نشان می‌دهد — با نام دقیق گزینه‌ها، همان‌طور که روی صفحهٔ خودِ آن دستگاه نوشته شده. برای ویندوز یک خط PowerShell آمادهٔ کپی هم هست.

**فایل PAC — یک آدرس به‌جای سه فیلد**
ویندوز و مک و iOS و اندروید همگی فیلد «آدرس پیکربندی خودکار پروکسی» دارند و گوشی حالا همین فایل را خودش می‌سازد. چون محتوایش دست خود ماست، آدرس‌های شبکهٔ محلی را از تونل مستثنا می‌کند — چاپگر و روتر و NAS بیهوده از گوشی رد نمی‌شوند — و روی همان یک پورت هم HTTP و هم SOCKS5 را پیشنهاد می‌دهد.

یک تصمیم عمدی: این فایل هرگز به حالت مستقیم برنمی‌گردد. PAC ای که موقع قطع شدن تونل مستقیم می‌فرستد، ترافیک دستگاه مقابل را دقیقاً در بدترین لحظه لخت بیرون می‌فرستد.

**جواب زندهٔ «آیا کار کرد؟» از هر دو طرف**
مشکل همیشگی هر راهنمای پروکسی این است که کاربر مراحل را می‌رود و نمی‌داند شد یا نه. حالا روی گوشی نوشته می‌شود «منتظر اولین دستگاه…» و به‌محض وصل شدن، آی‌پی همان دستگاه ظاهر می‌شود؛ و روی خود دستگاه مقابل، صفحهٔ راهنما هر دو ثانیه از گوشی می‌پرسد و سه حالت را نشان می‌دهد: هنوز تنظیم نشده، تنظیم شده ولی اتصالی دیده نمی‌شود، یا متصل. هیچ سرویس بیرونی در کار نیست.

**عیب‌یاب ده‌مرحله‌ای، هر ردیف با دکمهٔ رفعش**
«کار نمی‌کند» اینجا شش علت مختلف دارد که از بیرون همه شبیه هم‌اند. مهم‌ترین ردیف عیب‌یاب این است که آیا دستگاهی صفحهٔ راهنما را باز کرده یا نه، چون مسئله را دو نیم می‌کند: اگر باز کرده ولی وصل نشده، ایراد از تنظیمات خود آن دستگاه است؛ اگر اصلاً باز نکرده، دو دستگاه همدیگر را نمی‌بینند — که معمولاً یعنی وای‌فای کافه دستگاه‌هایش را از هم جدا نگه داشته و راه‌حلش هات‌اسپات خود گوشی است. خروجی گزارش قابل کپی هم هست.

**هات‌اسپات از داخل برنامه، با کد وای‌فای**
اگر گوشی روی هیچ شبکه‌ای نباشد، دکمهٔ هات‌اسپات همان‌جاست. نام و رمز را خود اندروید می‌سازد و کنارش یک QR وای‌فای می‌گذاریم که دوربین اندروید و آیفون مستقیم می‌خوانند — پس کسی لازم نیست رمزی را بلند بخواند. مجوز مکانی که اندروید برای هات‌اسپات لازم دارد فقط در همان لحظهٔ زدن دکمه خواسته می‌شود و دلیلش هم همان‌جا نوشته می‌شود. اگر گوشی اجازه نداد، دکمهٔ دوم مستقیم تنظیمات تترینگ اندروید را باز می‌کند.

**رمز پروکسی، مسدود کردن دستگاه، و مهلت اشتراک**
سه قابلیت اختیاری که هر سه پیش‌فرض خاموش‌اند. رمز پروکسی یک عدد شش رقمی خودکار است که هم SOCKS5 و هم HTTP را پوشش می‌دهد و خودبه‌خود داخل لینک راه‌اندازی می‌رود. مسدود کردن هر دستگاهی یک دکمه کنار همان ردیف است. مهلت اشتراک ۳۰ دقیقه یا یک یا دو ساعت می‌شود و بعدش خودکار قطع می‌شود — یک مهلت است نه کرونومتر، پس با بستن برنامه بی‌سروصدا تمدید نمی‌شود. و یک سوییچ چهارم: «فقط روی هات‌اسپات خودم»، که به‌محض رفتن روی وای‌فای دیگران پروکسی را دوباره روی خود گوشی می‌بندد.

**موتورهایی که اصلاً اشتراک‌گذاری ندارند دیگر وانمود نمی‌کنند**
MASQUE و وایرگارد و WARP-on-WARP در حالت VPN کل دستگاه را می‌گیرند و هیچ پروکسی محلی منتشر نمی‌کنند؛ وایرگارد آمنزیا و VPN Gate هم همین‌طور. حالا صفحه صریح می‌گوید موتور فعلی چه می‌تواند و چه نمی‌تواند، و برای سه تای اول دو راه کنار هم می‌گذارد: روشن کردن حالت پروکسی که همین موتور را با پروکسی بالا می‌آورد، یا رفتن سراغ موتوری دیگر. هیچ‌کدام خودکار انجام نمی‌شود.

**Tor و GST هم قابل اشتراک‌گذاری شدند**
لیسنر هر دوی این‌ها فقط روی خود گوشی باز می‌شد، پس صفحهٔ شبکه محلی یک اشتراک سالم را گزارش می‌داد که هیچ دستگاهی واقعاً نمی‌توانست به آن وصل شود. حالا هر دو وقتی اشتراک روشن باشد روی همهٔ رابط‌ها گوش می‌دهند.

**آدرس در پردهٔ اعلان‌ها، و یک کاشی تنظیمات سریع**
تا وقتی اشتراک روشن است، آدرس در یک اعلان می‌ماند با دو دکمه: کپی آدرس، و پایان اشتراک. دلیلش ساده است: کاربر معمولاً گوشی را یک دست دارد و با دست دیگر روی دستگاه مقابل تایپ می‌کند. یک کاشی تنظیمات سریع هم اضافه شد که زیرنویسش همان آدرس است.

**نقشهٔ مسیر و راهنمای شش سیستم‌عامل روی خود گوشی**
بالای صفحه چهار جعبه است — دستگاه مقابل، این گوشی، تونل، اینترنت — که هرکدام جداگانه روشن یا خاموش‌اند. عمداً نوار پیشرفت نیست: تونل می‌تواند قطع شود در حالی که هنوز دستگاهی وصل است. پایین صفحه هم راهنمای گام‌به‌گام ویندوز، مک، iOS، اندروید، لینوکس و تلویزیون/کنسول است.

**لیست دستگاه‌های متصل، بدون هیچ مجوزی**
روش معمول خواندن جدول ARP است که از اندروید ۱۰ به بعد برای برنامه‌های معمولی خالی برمی‌گردد. به‌جایش از جدول اتصال‌های TCP خودِ برنامه استفاده می‌کنیم — همان محدودیتی که ARP را خراب کرد اینجا باعث دقت می‌شود.

**هشداری که به شبکهٔ زیر پایتان نگاه می‌کند**
پروکسی اشتراکی رمز ندارد، ولی این روی هات‌اسپات خودتان یک معنی دارد و روی وای‌فای کافه یک معنی کاملاً دیگر. برنامه حالا از روی نام رابط شبکه تشخیص می‌دهد روی کدام هستید و فقط در حالت دوم هشدار می‌دهد. رفتار پیش‌فرض عمداً دست نخورده.

**عنوان تنظیمات عوض شد**
«اجازه اتصال شبکه محلی (Allow LAN)» شد «اتصال شبکه محلی»، و عنوان بالای صفحه‌اش «شبکه محلی». همهٔ متن‌های تازهٔ این بخش — صفحهٔ شبکه محلی، عیب‌یاب، و حتی صفحهٔ وبی که روی دستگاه مقابل باز می‌شود — هر دو زبانه هستند. فقط نام گزینه‌های ویندوز و مک و iOS ترجمه نشده‌اند، چون کاربر دنبال همان کلمه روی صفحه می‌گردد. اعداد هم همیشه لاتین می‌مانند.

---

### آنچه شدنی نبود

**مصرف به تفکیک شبکهٔ محلی.** `libv2ray.CoreController` فقط سه متد آماری دارد و هر سه outbound هستند. کلیدی که لازم بود از این wrapper در دسترس نیست، و از سمت outbound هم ترافیک خود گوشی و کلاینت‌ها روی یک outbound می‌نشینند. به‌جایش صفحه چیزی را نشان می‌دهد که واقعاً می‌داند: کدام دستگاه‌ها وصل‌اند و هرکدام چند اتصال باز دارند.

---

## Local Network — give another device this phone's connection

A new icon on the home screen that shares the phone's tunnelled connection with a laptop, TV or console — over Wi-Fi, a hotspot, or a USB cable, from whichever engine happens to be running.

- **Scan one QR code, type nothing.** The phone serves the instructions itself. The other device gets a page that works out from its own browser whether it is Windows, macOS, iPhone or Android and shows only those steps, with option names written exactly as they appear on that device. Windows also gets a one-line PowerShell command.
- **A PAC file.** One automatic-configuration URL instead of three fields. It keeps the local network off the tunnel and offers HTTP and SOCKS5 on one port. It never returns DIRECT — a PAC that falls back to a direct connection when the tunnel drops exposes the client at exactly the wrong moment.
- **A live "did it work?" answer from both ends**, read from the kernel's own connection table. No external service.
- **Ten-step diagnostics**, each row with the button that fixes it. The key row is whether any device fetched the setup page: it separates a client-side proxy mistake from Wi-Fi client isolation, which look identical otherwise.
- **A hotspot from inside the app**, with a Wi-Fi QR code both Android and iPhone cameras read directly. The location permission is asked for only at the tap, with the reason stated.
- **Proxy password, per-device blocking, and a share timer** — three optional protections, all off by default, plus an "only on my own hotspot" switch.
- **Engines that cannot share stop pretending they can.** MASQUE, WireGuard and WARP-on-WARP publish no local proxy in VPN mode; the screen says so and offers proxy mode or a different engine, neither automatically. **Tor and GST can now be shared** — both used to bind this phone only.
- **The address in the notification shade**, with copy and stop buttons, and a Quick Settings tile whose subtitle is the address.
- **A route diagram and six step-by-step guides on the phone**, for a device with no browser and for reading out to someone else.
- **A connected-device list with no permission at all**, from the app's own TCP table rather than the ARP table Android 10 emptied.
- **A warning that reads the network underneath** — your own hotspot or someone else's Wi-Fi. Default behaviour deliberately unchanged.
- **The settings entry was renamed** to "Local Network Connection", its page titled "Local Network". Every new string exists in both languages.

**Not shipped:** per-LAN usage figures. `libv2ray.CoreController` exposes only outbound stats, and on the outbound side the phone's own traffic and the clients' share one tag. The screen shows open connection counts per device instead, which it genuinely knows.

- Fix regressions introduced in the previous version.
- Change the name of the Quick Settings tile to app name.

- Improve file verification of the route asset updater (by [@lingyicute](https://github.com/lingyicute)). Before replacing the old files, for preset route asset providers, SHA-256 checksum is verified; for all files, the basic file structure is validated.
- Publish shortcuts dynamically to better work with some automation tools (#516, by [@lingyicute](https://github.com/lingyicute)).
- Many fixes for share link import and export (by [@lingyicute](https://github.com/lingyicute)).
- Fix connection failure caused by clearing the cache of the app.
- Fix some REALITY fingerprint values in UI not matching with the actual values.

- Update Go to 1.27.4 and ML-DSA is no longer advertised in `signature_algorithm_cert` in TLS Client Hello. Exclave's non-uTLS REALITY implementation also no longer advertises ML-DSA in `signature_algorithm_cert` to match the behavior of Go TLS.
- Update uTLS to latest commit and fingerprint "Chrome" now matches Chrome 155. uTLS latest commit requires Go 1.27, so Go 1.26 support is dropped and compiling Exclave now requires at least Go 1.27.
- For Snell protocol, domain address is no longer resolved to IP when sending UDP packets.
- Update Mozilla CA certificate store and 6 CA certificates are removed.
- The memory usage of rule matcher is reduced (maybe).

- Ignore certificates that can't be parsed by Go in AndroidCAstore (e.g. certificates with [negative serial number](https://crt.sh/?q=28903A635B5280FAE6774C0B6DA7D6BAA64AF2E8)).
- Fix chain proxy with the combination of some protocols unable to connect.
- Add [developer options](https://github.com/ExclaveNetwork/Exclave/wiki/Experiments) to set GODEBUG and environment variables for the Go library. They are set after Go runtime initialization, therefore not all GODEBUG and environment variables can take effect.
- Re-enable R8 optimizations for the legacy flavor.
- Update Java version from 21 to 25.

---

About CVE-2026-98432 ([NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/cve-2026-98432), [golang-announce](https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/PCoQcdxoScw)):

- Almost all the Linux kernels used by Android devices come without MPTCP support, so it is a no-op to disable MPTCP.
- Mitigating the vulnerability by disabling MPTCP is not the appropriate way. While the demonstrated exploit requires MPTCP, the underlying bug resides within TCP and is not specific to MPTCP. The fix for this vulnerability is to upgrade to a patched kernel version. Even if this vulnerability can be mitigated by disabling MPTCP, an outdated kernel is still vulnerable to tons of other RCE vulnerabilities.
- Therefore, Exclave will not explicitly disable MPTCP like many other proxy software and network tools written in Go.
- If you did compile the kernel with MPTCP support, or you insist that MPTCP must be explicitly disabled like some other Go-written software, set the related GODEBUG value through developer options yourself.

- Fix high CPU usage after proxy closed or network switching for Hysteria 2 (maybe other QUIC-based protocols too).
- Fix connections not closed correctly on proxy closed.
- Fix the `/proc/net/` based UID dumper on Android 9 or earlier (similar to https://github.com/SagerNet/sing-box/commit/40bc411e8d024e3f8c8f435c2a2ad5e4c0e04bce).

- Add experimental CONNECT-IP (so-called "MASQUE") support.
- Fix CONNECT-UDP bugs.
- Update Go to 1.27.3, which has been hardcoded to blacklist 8 eMudhra intermediate certificates.
- Update the bundled Mozilla CA certificate store to the latest version, which has removed eMudhra root certificates.
- Rename root CA provider "system" to "Go" and rename root CA provider "system and user" to "Android" to avoid confusion.

This is a security update. The private keys for some of eMudhra’s intermediate certificates are too weak, causing them to be [compromised](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/) through enumeration and exposing users to man-in-the-middle attacks. These private keys have since spread across the Internet and can be obtained by everyone.

You may want to know the impact of the compromise of eMudhra intermediate certificates for Exclave: https://github.com/ExclaveNetwork/Exclave/issues/500.

# ArasClient 1.9.0

These APKs were compiled and signed by this workflow run, from the
pinned sources — not copied off a developer machine. Take the file
that matches your phone; the universal build installs anywhere and is
the largest.

## What changed

Since `v1.8.97`:

### New
- Four app themes, picked during onboarding and switchable in Settings
- First-run coach-mark guide that spotlights the real controls instead of text pages
- Jalali (Persian) dates for subscription expiry

### Improved
- Subscription tab rail and two-column config cards rebuilt in the PattNG style
- Ping results are color-coded by delay; tap the stop icon to cancel a running test
- Bottom bar text shrinks to fit instead of truncating
- Unified corner radius across cards and bars; cleaner menus and insets

### Under the hood
- New xray core (patterniha v26.11.21) with Serverless-for-Iran v62 support

2. Allow installs from unknown sources for the app you downloaded with.

## ArasClient v1.8.6

- **Warm-up listener fix** — a kept-connection SOCKS5 greeting probe counts each served listener once, so long Psiphon/Tor warm-ups no longer queue up on connection attempts

releases.title: ArasClient v1.8.2
releases.notes:
# ArasClient v1.8.2

Two rounds since **v1.8.1**: the ECH (Encrypted Client Hello) work for the
Xray profiles, and WireGuard/AmneziaWG dialled by the core like every other
protocol. Everything from v1.8.1 and earlier is described in the
[v1.8.1 release notes](https://github.com/ArasTey/ArasClient/releases/tag/v1.8.1).

## 🕵️ ECH: the key lookup can now ride through its own outbound

Plain-DNS ECH key lookups are being blocked in some places while ECH itself
still works (cloudflare-ech.com answers). The lookup needs a path of its own,
and the app now has one:

- **Two fields on TLS profiles** (VMess / VLESS / Shadowsocks / Trojan, and
  Hysteria2): `echConfigList` — the key source — and **`echOutbound`**, the ECH
  outbound as raw JSON. The Aether profiles keep their own ECH fields (ECH DNS
  / ECH domain) from v1.8.1; this one is for the Xray protocols.
- **The recipe** (from the core's author):

  ```json
  echConfigList: h2c://1.1.1.1/dns-query
  ```

  ```json
  echOutbound:
  {"tag":"tls-repack-dns","protocol":"freedom","settings":{"redirect":"1.1.1.1:443"},"streamSettings":{"security":"tls","tlsSettings":{"serverName":"www.microsoft.com","verifyPeerCertByName":"fromMitm,www.microsoft.com","alpn":["fromMitm"],"fingerprint":"chrome"}}}
  ```

- **What the app does with it**: the ECH outbound is appended to the generated
  configuration exactly as written, and the profile's TLS settings get
  `echSockopt.dialerProxy` pointing at it — so the ECH key query leaves
  through that masked outbound (a TLS connection to a public resolver with a
  borrowed SNI and a certificate checked by name) instead of a plain DNS
  query. The profile's own handshake then uses the fetched key, and the real
  server name stays hidden.
- **The guards**: the ECH outbound must be a JSON object, must come with an
  echConfigList, and needs a tag of its own — not `direct`, `block` or
  `exit-node`, and not starting with `proxy` (balancers pick their members by
  that prefix). Two different ECH outbounds written under the same tag get
  numbered (`tag-2`); a tag another outbound already uses is refused; an
  imported ECH outbound that was never checked fails the connection instead of
  letting the query go out in the clear. The ECH outbound is a TLS-only
  setting — a REALITY profile keeps it unused. Same rules as PattNG P67.
- **No core rebuild was needed**: the bundled Xray core (patterniha v26.10.13)
  already carries the ECH-over-h2c lookup, the `echSockopt` and the `fromMitm`
  certificate-by-name support — the app-side plumbing was the missing half.

## 🔌 WireGuard and AmneziaWG, dialled by the core like every other protocol

- **AmneziaWG was bypassing the core.** The selected AWG profile took the
  VpnService TUN descriptor for itself, so the tunnel came up carrying nothing:
  no DNS, no routing, no statistics — while the latency test of the same
  profile went through the core. The standalone tunnel is gone: every
  protocol, AmneziaWG included, is dialled by the core now, and the TUN has one
  reader again.
- **Plain WireGuard** had no keep-alive (the peer's mapping expires after
  minutes) and left `noKernelTun` unset — in root mode the core then built a
  kernel TUN that fought the app's own interface. Both are filled in now, with
  the allowed IPs and the keep-alive.
- **The `.conf` parsers** no longer cut an IPv6 endpoint in half and no longer
  drop `PersistentKeepalive`.

## 🔧 In this release

- The bundled core AAR was rebuilt from the same pinned core tag
  (`aras-core-26.10.13`); the core source itself did not change.
- The five APKs are the same size as v1.8.1's (the ECH work is a few lines of
  code; the rebuilt core library differs by 40 KB).

## 🔐 Signing

- Signed with the dedicated ArasClient key — **the same key as v1.7.10 and
  v1.8.1** (certificate SHA-256 `3b2a6fa9…b5ba`): all five APKs, one signer
  each. Upgrades install over v1.8.1 without uninstalling.

## ⚠️ Known limitations

- The ECH outbound is used on TLS profiles only, and the recipe's `fromMitm`
  certificate check relies on the core's fromMitm support — present in the
  bundled core.
- Profiles imported with a broken older build keep wrong AWG values: config
  fixes change parsing, not stored data. If AWG still fails after updating,
  **delete the profile and re-import the `.conf` file**.
- **OpenVPN is not included.** The official path is integrating with the
  installed OpenVPN for Android via its intent/AIDL API — planned as its own
  release.
- The Psiphon/Aether/Mieru tunnel path is not re-verified on a device for this
  release's cores yet (the network blocked handshakes during testing; the old
  and the new cores behaved identically under the same conditions, so no
  regression is suspected).
- Release builds log at `warning` level by default — set the log level to Info
  in Settings before reporting a VPN problem.

releases.title: ArasClient v1.8.1
releases.notes:
# ArasClient v1.8.1

Everything below is **every change since v1.7.10** — the releases v1.8.0 and
v1.8.1 listed in one place. v1.8.1 on top of v1.8.0 fixes the delay numbers,
and adds the exit node, sing-box imports and the TLS fingerprints.

## 🛜 AmneziaWG actually works now (the headline of 1.8.0)

AmneziaWG profiles **never carried traffic** before v1.8.0. Five defects were
stacked to hide it, all fixed:

1. **Mimic packets (I1–I5) reach the core.** Decoys sent ahead of every
   handshake initiation so the first bytes on the wire belong to another
   protocol (e.g. an "OPTIONS sip:…" line). Configured per profile in the AWG
   editor; a spec the core cannot parse fails validation at edit time instead
   of silently killing the tunnel at connect.
2. **Junk params are read from `[Interface]`.** AmneziaVPN writes
   `Jc/Jmin/Jmax/S1/S2/H1–H4` as device-level settings; the old parser read
   them in peer context, found nothing, and silently substituted stock values
   — the server dropped every packet. Now `[Interface]` first, `[Peer]`
   fallback.
3. **`.conf` detection no longer depends on the exact spelling of `Jc`.**
   Files are classified as Amnezia on the key set, case-insensitively
   (including S3/S4 and I1–I5).
4. **The TUN descriptor has one reader.** tun2socks used to win the race and
   drain packets into a SOCKS proxy nothing serves in AWG mode.
5. **An entry proxy that is Aether/Mieru no longer marks a whole subscription
   −1.** The daemons now start when a chain needs them (refcounted), and the
   latency test no longer probes a chained profile's server directly.

Verified end-to-end on an emulator: tunnel up, junk params matching the file,
mimic packets emitted, traffic crossing the tun interface across repeated
on/off cycles.

## 📶 Ping and delay fixes (the point of 1.8.1)

- **Delay numbers read ~5× too high in v1.8.0 — fixed.** A v1.8.0 change made
  every measurement a single cold request: it paid the wireguard handshake +
  TCP + TLS (≈4–5 round trips) instead of one round trip on a warm
  connection. A server whose real delay was ~100 ms displayed ~500 ms.
  The measurement is back to the v1.7.x semantics: two samples over the same
  connection, min kept — the first warms the path, the second reads one real
  RTT.
- **"Ping all" reports the egress country on cards now.** A new core shim
  carries the country/IP back through the same dial path as the delay test,
  so batch results fill the card flags without separate requests.
- **Tests start immediately** instead of waiting behind a GeoIP pre-warm
  (DNS + batch lookup) that used to run before the first ping was dispatched.
- **No more dropped frames during long test runs.** Each result patches its
  own card; the whole group is no longer rebuilt (and every profile
  re-decoded) once per result.

## 📝 Remarks are yours

- **Provider flags in remarks are kept** on import: nothing rewrites a
  non-empty remark any more; default names only fill an empty one. Cards
  still compose their own flag, so nothing renders twice.

## 🚪 Exit node (new in 1.8.1)

In the Aether editor you can now pick **which config the tunnel dials out
through** — the list shows your profiles, the same way a proxy chain does:

- Leave it blank and the tunnel leaves directly (freedom), as always.
- Name a profile and the aether core's own dialer goes through the app's core
  to that profile's outbound — a chain pinned to the exit side.
- A name that no longer matches exactly one profile never breaks the
  connect: it degrades to the direct exit, and the editor shows what it
  picked.
- Latency tests of exit-node profiles serialize, because each owns the loop
  back port while it runs.

## 🧩 Core updated to patterniha v26.10.13

The bundled Xray core moved to patterniha's v26.10.13 base with our AmneziaWG
patches carried over (+91 upstream commits over v1.8.0's base), notably:

- **TUN inbound** uses Xray's built-in lightweight TCP/IP stack (gVisor
  removed) with several stability fixes.
- **MASQUE**: XMUX support, WARP domain-fronting fixes, Chrome User-Agent.
- **TLS**: Xray's built-in RootCAs by default (defends against a maliciously
  injected system CA), more ECH hardening.
- **Lua scripting** for `dns` and `routing` (power users).
- `allowInsecure` keeps working on public servers (restored for legacy
  profiles since the 26.x cores removed it).
- The fingerprint picker gains `hellochrome_120/131/133`,
  `hellofirefox_120/148`.

## 🌐 Root mode

- **DNS leak fix for LAN-to-ISP resolvers** (ported from upstream #6298): DNS
  queries to private/LAN resolvers are DNAT'd to a public IP so they resolve
  through the configured remote DNS instead of leaking back to the LAN/ISP
  resolver — the "some sites work, some don't" symptom.

## 🪂 Aether core updated to the official v2.3.0

`libaether.so` (arm64 / armeabi-v7a / x86_64) now carries the official
CluvexStudio Aether v2.3.0 release binaries, checksums verified against the
release's SHA256SUMS.txt. With it, and matching PattNG's editor:

- **MASQUE SNI** — the name the MASQUE handshakes put in their ClientHello.
- **Encrypted Client Hello (ECH)** with its lookup resolver (`ECH DNS`) and
  key domain (`ECH domain`).
- **Four TLS fingerprints** — Chrome (default), Firefox, Semi-Python, Go:
  the core offers the captured client's TLS 1.2 suite order and drops GREASE
  where that client sends none.
- **WireGuard-over-MASQUE (gool)**, **MASQUE-in-MASQUE (mim)**, **WARP-in-WARP
  (wiw)** — two-hop tunnels with outer and inner gateways, as before.
- **warp→Psiphon, Psiphon→warp, Psiphon-only** — the three carrier modes,
  with Psiphon region support.
- The **exit node** picker above is an Aether editor feature too.

## 📥 sing-box subscriptions (.json) now import

An update to a sing-box `.json` sublink used to import nothing. The
converter reads the dialing outbounds — **vless** (including REALITY's
public key / short id / fingerprint), **vmess**, **trojan**,
**shadowsocks**, **hysteria2** — into the same share links the app has al-
ways read, skips group/meta objects (selector, urltest, direct, block, dns),
and validates the whole list before touching storage. Manual imports and
subscription updates both take it.

## 🔧 Infrastructure & fixes

- **Release signing restored in CI** — the workflow step that restores the
  keystore was missing the secrets mapping since the key hardening, so every
  automated build had failed with `KEYSTORE_B64: unbound variable`. CI now
  builds, signs, and uploads end-to-end (verified green).
- The main menu sheet (the three-line menu) no longer bounces up and down
  when dragged hard; it is pinned to the expanded position with an inner
  scroll.
- Subscription traffic display accepts a `used=` key, which some panels send
  instead of `upload`/`download`.
- This release is signed with the dedicated ArasClient key — **the same key
  as v1.7.10** and every release before it that carried it: all five APKs,
  one signer each. Upgrades install without uninstalling.

## ⚠️ Known limitations

- **Profiles imported with a broken older build keep wrong AWG values.**
  Config fixes change parsing, not stored data. If AWG still fails after
  updating: **delete the profile and re-import the `.conf` file.**
- **OpenVPN is not included.** The official path is integrating with the
  installed OpenVPN for Android via its intent/AIDL API — planned as its own
  release.
- The bundled Psiphon server list (427 entries) is verified against
  Psiphon's signing key on every use, and the client fetches a fresh list
  itself once it has network. The full Psiphon/Aether/Mieru tunnel path is
  not re-verified on a device for this release's new cores yet (the network
  blocked handshakes during testing; the old and new cores behaved
  identically under the same conditions, so no regression is suspected).
- Release builds log at `warning` level by default — set the log level to
  Info in Settings before reporting a VPN problem.

releases.title: ArasClient v1.7.10
releases.notes:
ArasClient v1.7.10

Adds Mieru gateway profiles and rebuilds the connect button. The core is unchanged from v1.7.9.

### Persian layout

The top bar draws the wordmark as two texts — "Aras" and "Client" — side by side in a row. In a
Persian layout that row lays out right to left, so the halves swapped and the title read
**"ClientAras"**. The wordmark is now pinned left to right: a brand reads the same in every language.
Where the app name appears as a single string it is wrapped in a directional isolate instead, and
deliberately not where it builds a file name, since those marks would otherwise end up in the path.

**134 strings had no Persian translation**, so the whole Aether and Mieru editor, the `.arasc` export
screen, the stats screen and the menu sections fell back to English inside a Persian interface. All
134 are translated; the Persian locale now carries every string the default one does.

### Mieru

Mieru is a separate client process that holds the tunnel and serves a local SOCKS, so a Mieru
profile is carried by a SOCKS hop to that listener — the same shape an Aether profile already has.
No core work was needed: Mieru ships a native Android build.

- Add a Mieru profile manually from the import menu, or import a `mieru://` link
- Round-trips through `.arasc` like every other profile type
- The client is taken from enfein/mieru v3.38.0, checksum verified against the release

**A Mieru client left behind by a killed app is now reaped before a start.** This is not tidiness: a
survivor keeps the loopback port, and the next start then dies with `address already in use` rather
than starting at all.

**Mieru is arm64 only.** That is the only Android build published, so the editor reports the client as
absent on an `armeabi-v7a` or `x86_64` device rather than failing obscurely. It adds about 14 MB to
the arm64 split.

### Connect button

The connect button is rebuilt. It was a flat rounded box that distinguished connected from stopped by
nothing but the glyph changing.

Everything that glows is now drawn inside the circle: the rotating sweep is inset to the rim and
clipped by the shape, and the breathing light is a radial gradient that is transparent in the middle.
Nothing spills past the outline, so the button keeps a clean edge against the bar behind it.

The rotation and the breath run only while the tunnel is up, and the entry spring fires once on the
way to connected, so an idle button costs nothing.

### Size

The arm64 split is about 52 MB and the universal about 140 MB. The other splits are unchanged.

### Tests

178. The Mieru configuration is checked by parsing it: a password containing a quote, a backslash and
a newline has to come back out exactly as it went in.

Still nothing here has been through a device test. If something misbehaves, the app's logcat screen
carries the Mieru client's own output.

releases.title: ArasClient v1.7.9
releases.notes:
ArasClient v1.7.9

A large release: the native core moves to patterniha/Xray-core v26.9.27, MASQUE and the
xdrive transport arrive, and Aether gateway profiles are supported end to end.

### Core

The core is rebuilt on patterniha/Xray-core v26.9.27, with every ArasClient patch carried
over: AnyTLS, the AmneziaWG 3.1 junk parameters, `allowInsecure` as a TLS field, and the
`domain_strategy` field that AmneziaWG needs. This is 26 patch releases of upstream work,
plus the MASQUE and xdrive transports, which the old 26.9.1 base predated.

### Fixed

Five config-generation bugs, each caught by tests added in this release:

- **AnyTLS did not work at all.** The outbound was emitted with a `tcp` transport and no
  `anytlsSettings`, because the transport was set where `populateTransportSettings`
  immediately overwrote it. AnyTLS now emits its own transport.
- **AmneziaWG obfuscation was missing on first connect.** The junk parameters were copied
  onto the peer before the defaults were applied to the profile, so a server that had never
  been saved with them tunnelled unobfuscated.
- **One malformed port could break every server.** A non-numeric or out-of-range port threw
  out of config generation, and its callers only guarded a null return — so a bad server in a
  policy group or chain took the whole configuration down. It is now skipped.
- **Hysteria2 share links lost their bandwidth limits** and the port-hopping interval.
- **AmneziaWG's H3 parameter vanished on share and import.**

When the core rejects a configuration, its own reason now reaches the screen instead of a
generic "failed to start", and the generated configuration is written to the log at error
level so a rejection is diagnosable from a release build.

### MASQUE and xdrive

`MASQUE` (IETF CONNECT-IP, RFC 9484) is supported and import-only: it arrives through a
`masque://` link, a pasted config, a QR code or a `.arasc` file, and is deliberately not in
the "Add manually" list. The `masque` and `xdrive` transports are in the transport picker of
any protocol that supports them.

### Aether

Aether gateway profiles are supported. The tunnel is dialled by the aether core, a child
process holding the WARP identity and the scanned endpoint, so a profile's outbound is a SOCKS
hop to its loopback listener. The core ships in the app as a native library, checksum-verified
against its release, together with Psiphon's client and Tor's pluggable transport.

Share links and `.arasc` files use aether's own vocabulary, so they move between ArasClient,
the Aether app and PattNG unchanged. The screen collects the protocol (WireGuard, MASQUE, or
either two-hop tunnel), scan mode, obfuscation, IP version, ClientHello fragmentation, ECH,
and Psiphon and Tor. Two pairings the core refuses are caught while editing rather than at
connect time: either carrier in reverse needs MASQUE, and the two go together only nested.

**A WARP gateway usually does not answer a plain ping, and its exit address reads as Iranian.
Both are expected** — judge these profiles by whether they connect, not by the ping column.

**This release is larger than usual: about 54 MB of native library per ABI.**

### Build and tests

CI previously assembled the release APK and nothing else — the test suite never ran. It now
runs the unit tests and lint, and asserts against the built core that AnyTLS and AmneziaWG are
present and stock WireGuard is not, since a patch that fails to apply still produces a working
library, just one missing a feature. The core checkout is pinned by tag, so a release builds
the same core it was tested against.

The suite grew from 17 tests to 170.

releases.title: ArasClient v1.7.5
releases.notes:
## What's Changed

ArasClient v1.7.5 brings the accumulated subscription, connectivity, diagnostics, and Quick Settings improvements developed since v1.7.0.

### Subscription Management

- Added a selected-subscription action that updates the subscription, runs a real ping test, sorts the results, and connects to the fastest reachable server.
- Added **Ping all in this subscription** directly to the selected subscription action box beside Edit, Update, Copy, and Delete.
- Improved Clash YAML parsing, including configuration-key ordering and UTF-8 BOM handling.
- Corrected Shadowsocks parsing for configurations using the `v2ray-plugin` option.
- Made Free-subscription replacement transactional so an interrupted update does not leave a partially replaced profile set.
- Improved subscription import/export handling, profile replacement, URL/clipboard import flows, and subscription navigation.
- Added shared subscription-workflow locking so update operations cannot race across the UI and daemon processes.
- Improved Free-subscription synchronization and reduced repeated failed retry work with a persisted cooldown.

### Connection Diagnostics

- Persist the real connection-ping delay, country code, IP address, and test timestamp for each profile.
- Prefer the country measured by the current connection ping on profile cards, with GeoIP and configuration-name fallbacks when no current measurement is available.
- Improved country/flag resolution and legacy serialization compatibility.
- Added unit coverage for country persistence, legacy delay records, and ping-country precedence.

### Quick Settings

- Added a complete **Update & Connect** Quick Settings workflow with progress, completion, and failure states.
- Added clear, distinct iconography for the Connect/Disconnect and Update/Connect actions.
- Made Update/Connect a true toggle: a second tap stops the running workflow and connected client and returns the tile to its ready state.
- Made Connect/Disconnect follow the actual core state, show the running server while connected, and return to an inactive state when stopped.
- Corrected Quick Settings service discovery metadata and preserved active state across tile-service recreation.
- Kept the launcher shortcut path as an additional quick-access route.

### Reliability and Performance

- Prevented duplicate Activity initialization work during recreation.
- Improved subscription update cancellation and daemon workflow cleanup.
- Improved card-rendering performance and reduced unnecessary UI work during subscription and connection updates.
- Preserved existing VPN, proxy, root, browser-dialer, and AmneziaWG functionality while extending the Quick Actions workflow.

### Documentation

- Updated the project README and release-facing documentation for the new subscription and Quick Actions capabilities.

### Validation

- Debug and release APK builds pass.
- The full debug unit-test suite passes.
- Release lintVital passes.
- All release variants are generated for arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86, x86_64, and universal APK delivery.
- The GitHub release workflow rebuilds the native core bindings and release APKs from the configured upstream sources before attaching the artifacts.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ArasTey/ArasClient/compare/v1.7.0...v1.7.5

**The last way out (Tor) is off until you allow it, on every system and in every store edition.**

- "When nothing else works: the Tor network" no longer shows on from the first start. Tor never carried anything before the user said yes, but the switch looked as if it was on; it now shows what the user chose.

releases.notes:
## Shroudly 2.6.89

**"Your own server" takes VLESS and Trojan links, on every platform.**

### Every platform (Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, Android TV, iPhone, iPad, the Mac App Store app, Apple TV)
- Your own server now takes `vless://` and `trojan://` links, the kinds people in Iran pass around, where Shadowsocks is filtered by its look (asked for from Iran, with a link to a server behind a CDN). Carried over plain TCP, a WebSocket or HTTPUpgrade, with TLS or without; `host`, `sni`, `path` and `alpn` are read from the link, and Xray's `?ed=` note is taken off the path. Shroudly has no servers of its own: the server is the user's, as with Shadowsocks.
- A link that asks for something not carried is told so by its name, never tried another way: REALITY, the XTLS Vision flow, gRPC, XHTTP, mKCP, VLESS's own encryption.
- The server's certificate is checked for the name the link gives (its `sni`, or its `Host`, or its address). A certificate that is not valid for it is refused and said as that. `allowInsecure=1` is followed on the desktop only; on phones, tablets and Apple devices such a link is refused with its name.
- The saved link is shown with its key covered, and the log never has it.

### Windows, macOS, Linux (updates)
- An update (about 100 MB) is no longer downloaded by itself while the Roblox player is open or a full-screen program is in front. On a thin line it took the whole line for minutes, and a game's delay went from tens of milliseconds to seconds "out of nowhere" (a report from an ADSL line, 13 Mbit/s down). It is looked at again at each check, so the download comes once the game is over; "Check for updates" by hand downloads at once, as before.

### Every platform (the engine)
- Plain HTTP: the technique that rewrites the Host header writes it in mixed case (`hOsT:`) instead of all lower case (`host:`). A filter that looks for `Host:` often looks for `host:` too, which every HTTP/2 client writes: Vietnam's resets both and lets the mixed case through (measured from a Vietnamese line on 2026-11-22, where the technique opened none of four blocked sites before and all four after). Every one of 96 large web servers answered the mixed case exactly as the usual one.

### Tests
- The headers are the same bytes on every platform (`tests/net/fixtures/vless-vectors.json`, read by the desktop's, Android's and Apple's tests). Each platform carries connections through a server of each kind written in its tests (TCP, WebSocket, HTTPUpgrade; the desktop and Android also with TLS); Apple's TLS is tried against a real site by its name, by its address with the name in `sni`, and under a name its certificate is not for.
- The Windows lab's stand-in DNS forwarder takes a port the system picks and is waited for: on a port of the lab's choosing it sometimes never came up, and the DNS gate was reported as not answering.

releases.title: Shroudly v2.6.88
releases.notes:
## Shroudly 2.6.88

**Windows: Advanced mode asks for the administrator's permission once, not at every start of the computer; Games and apps mode comes on even when Windows is slow at startup; an antivirus that blocks PowerShell no longer gets it started over and over.**

### Windows (Advanced mode)
- Every start of the Advanced engine was a permission prompt (UAC, "shroudly-core-adv.exe"): at every start of the computer, and again whenever the engine had ended. Since 2.6.87 a game or a Stop no longer ends it; now the prompt itself is answered once. The engine started through it copies itself and WinDivert's files to `Common Files\Shroudly\advanced`, a folder only an administrator can write, and registers a scheduled task that runs that copy for this user only, on demand. From then on Shroudly starts Advanced mode through the task, with no prompt. It asks again, once, only after an update that changed the engine, or when the task is gone; whatever goes wrong on this way (a policy, an antivirus) ends in the prompt, as before.
- What the engine started this way does is not the caller's to say: it takes its options from a request file and accepts only the packet options, each checked; it writes its status only into its own folder, a new file every time; in the user's folder it only reads. Uninstalling Shroudly removes the task and the copies.
- The engine opens no console window of its own.
- A prompt nobody answered for three minutes (the computer started with no one at it) is said as that; it used to read "Advanced mode failed: #< CLIXML".

### Windows (Games and apps mode, Roblox)
- On a computer still starting up, with an antivirus looking at every new program, Windows' registry tool took longer than its four seconds, and Games and apps mode was refused for the whole session ("this session has no volatile environment"): Roblox opened with no way to the internet ("critical settings could not be downloaded", a report from Türkiye). The engine now reads and writes those settings itself when the tool does not answer in time (after two such waits the tool is not tried again in that run), and where even that fails the mode is tried again by itself after 8 s, 30 s, 90 s and 5 minutes.
- An antivirus that blocks PowerShell's command line (Avast) showed its warning over and over: a Roblox program being judged was asked about every two seconds, each time in a new PowerShell. After four questions in a row without an answer none is started for ten minutes, then for longer and longer, until it answers again; said once in the log.

### Windows, macOS (Games and apps mode)
- NO_PROXY no longer ends with the IPv6 ranges `fc00::/7` and `fe80::/10`: Python's httpx reads each entry as a URL and failed on them ("Invalid port: ':'"), so Unsloth Studio and every tool built on httpx would not start while the mode was on (#96). The value an earlier version wrote is replaced when the mode comes on, and still removed as ours.

### Windows, macOS, Linux
- A computer that does not let Shroudly create files (a cleaning program that removed the temporary folder, folders protected against new files): the temporary folder is made again, and what was refused is said once with what to do, instead of "ENOENT" at every step.

## Shroudly 2.6.85

**Advanced mode against a connection cut after its first kilobytes: a site that opens and then stops (x.com and Discord's app on Rostelecom) gets the stronger way on its next connections, and on Windows its decoys can now be kept from servers by TCP timestamps.**

releases.notes:
## Shroudly 2.6.83

**Blocked sites open faster: a new one starts with what already opened other blocked sites on the network, the names of one service share what one of them finds, and a technique that keeps working is not checked again after a restart; new techniques (several TLS records, random-size segments, an urgent byte with a record cut, new cut places in the domain's own label, HTTP Host rewrites); Advanced mode gets a stronger way for servers nothing else opens and steps aside before a game's anti-cheat looks; remote settings fall back to their mirror.**

### Every system
- A blocked site the engine had never seen started with the untouched request, and behind a filter that drops without a word that was a second or more of silence before any technique, then the list a batch at a time, for every new name (a report from Türk Telekom: blocked sites opened visibly later than with a tool that applies one fixed method to everything, while the line itself was as fast through Shroudly as without it). Now, once one technique has opened two different blocked sites on this network, a new name races it against the untouched request: the untouched request still goes first with a short moment to itself, so a site that is not blocked goes untouched as before. It is forgotten when the network changes, and nothing is learned from it unless the untouched request is shown blocked.
- Names of one site or service opened at once share what one of them finds (YouTube's video servers and images, Discord's domains, Instagram's, X's), instead of each walking the list on its own.
- A learned technique is checked again half an hour after it last opened the site, not half an hour after it was learned: after a restart or a network change, sites learned earlier no longer race the untouched request on their first connection. A block that was lifted is still found.
- New techniques in Auto, at the end of the list so nothing before them moves: an urgent byte after the first and the record cut five bytes before the name's end (what many Türk Telekom users run), the same cut after a one-byte split, and a record cut in the middle of the domain's own label. New cut places for that label (googlevideo in rr3---sn-x.googlevideo.com), where a cut in the middle of a long CDN name fell in the subdomain. A batch of the search holds one more technique, so a name nothing opens still reaches the last way out no later than before.
- New fixed choices in Settings, applied to every site from the first packet: several TLS records, small random pieces, an urgent byte with a record cut. They are not in Auto's list: every technique added there is one more a site nothing opens walks before the last way out.
- Plain HTTP: Host header rewrites every server tried took (lower-case header name, mixed-case host, no space), tried only on HTTP connections.
- A newly opened blocked site's line says how long it took ("opened with X (3 tries, ipv4, 2.4 s)").
- Remote settings ask each source in turn until one gives a usable file: a file whose signature does not check (a mirror out of step, a captive portal's page), expired or older no longer ends the check at the first source.

### Windows, macOS and Linux
- Advanced mode steps aside as soon as a game's anti-cheat bootstrapper starts (Fortnite's launcher and Easy Anti-Cheat's _EAC_EOS program; BattlEye's _BE launchers): it used to wait for the service and the game to be seen together, after the anti-cheat had already scanned the drivers, and Fortnite kicked a player for a "forbidden tool".
- Advanced mode: a server whose decoyed first segment goes out again unanswered gets a stronger way for ten minutes: the decoy eight times, kept from the server by the TCP timestamp where the connection has one, and the real ClientHello cut after its first byte with the decoy's ClientHello in front of it (what opened YouTube's video servers on Rostelecom). Every other server goes exactly as before; the seqovl part is never larger than the real segment, for PPPoE lines.

### Android
- An update download that timed out on every source is tried once more through the engine, then directly.

## Shroudly 2.6.82

**Tor starts again on Android; with QUIC off, calls and games on UDP 443 go through again; no country taken from a remembered shutdown where the time zone names another; signed remote settings, so a technique, a Tor bridge or a rule can change without a new version; the store copies follow the stores' rules on helping others.** (2.6.81 was not released on its own: everything of it is here.)

### Android
- The last way out (Tor) ended with code 1 at once on phones after 2.6.80 (Tor 16.0.1 there); Android is back on Tor 16.0, which ran on them, while the computers keep 16.0.1. Tor's own warnings and errors now go into the log, a few a start, so a failure says why.

### Android, iPhone, iPad and the Mac
- QUIC turned off dropped every datagram to UDP port 443, which cut what uses that port for itself, calls' relays among them (WhatsApp calls stuck on "connecting"). Now only a flow that starts as QUIC is turned away (its Initial answered, as in 2.6.80); anything else on 443 goes as any UDP does.

### Every system
- Remote settings: Shroudly reads remote.json from its repository (through itself while protection is on, from GitHub or its jsDelivr mirror) every six hours. It is data, never code, and is used only when its ECDSA P-256 signature checks against the key every app carries, its number is higher than the one in use and it has not expired; the last good one is kept. It can change, by platform, country and version: the techniques the engine starts with (an allow-list: never a server, a file, a port or an address), the decoy names, Tor's bridges or whether Tor starts at all, the phones' default for "Turn off QUIC" (a choice the user made stays), and when "Something not working?" shows. A new one takes effect at once.
- The Android Tor bundle is now checked at build time for libraries no Android has: 16.0.1's asked for libz.so.1, which is why Tor never started on phones in 2.6.80.
- A country remembered from a shutdown is used only where the time zone names no place (UTC and the like), and a site of a listed country answering alone counts as a national-only network only where the time zone is that country's: a phone in Qatar had kept Iranian decoy names.
- Where torproject.org is cut, the computers fetch Tor 16.0.1 from its mirror on Shroudly's GitHub again (the mirror for 16.0.1 was missing in 2.6.80).

### Google Play, the App Store and TestFlight
- "Help people in censored countries" inside Shroudly (a Snowflake proxy for the Tor network) is left out of the store copies: Google Play and the App Store take an app that lets other people use the device as a proxy only when that is what the app is for. The link to Psiphon's Conduit, an app made for it, stays. The APK and the IPA from GitHub, and the desktop, keep it as before. Ad blocking on Android was already only in the APK from GitHub.

releases.title: Shroudly v2.6.80
releases.notes:
## Shroudly 2.6.80

**QUIC turned off is refused on the spot on every system; the country is read from the time zone first; "Something not working?" only after Shroudly itself went wrong; a Roblox installer from the browser goes through Shroudly by itself; Tor 16.0.1.**

### Every system
- QUIC turned off (the default on phones, "QUIC to TCP" in the desktop's Advanced mode): an app's or a program's QUIC Initial is now answered on the spot with a Version Negotiation that offers no real version, so it gives QUIC up at once and uses TCP. Dropped unanswered, apps first waited for QUIC's own timeout: Instagram's comments opened late, or minutes later, in Turkey. On Android, iPhone, iPad and the Mac the engine answers it; on Windows and Linux in Advanced mode the packet layer does. Nothing of it goes out to the network, as before.
- The country Shroudly takes you to be in (its decoy names, the national-network check) is now read from the time zone first, and only then from a shutdown seen before; a site of another country answering alone no longer counts as a national-only network. One had made a phone in Turkey "Iranian" for good.

- "Something not working?" shows only after Shroudly itself went wrong (protection could not start, the engine ended or stuck, apps or browsers not getting through it), for a day, and goes again once a report is sent; in every country. A network down, a blocked address or a refused permission does not count.
- Tor 16.0.1 (was 16.0) on Windows, macOS, Linux and Android, with the Snowflake and bridge fixes it brings.

### Desktop
- A Roblox installer started from the browser, before Roblox is installed, goes around the system proxy; on a network that blocks Roblox (by DNS or otherwise) it failed. Shroudly now checks at once when it sees one running, turns Games and apps mode on where Roblox is blocked, and starts the installer again through itself.

### Android, iPhone, iPad and the Mac
- When the system ends Shroudly to save memory or battery while protection is on and starts it again, the log now says so; a report showed only the engine starting over and over (Roblox during a WhatsApp call).
- Android: the explanation under "Only listed sites" is behind its title's (i), as every other section's, and About no longer repeats Settings (the bar's gear opens them; issue #47). The Play build carries androidx.fragment 1.9.1.

## Shroudly 2.6.75

**Tor only when it is the answer; every technique on the first visit; http:// sites that the network drops without a word; apps that keep addresses after a network change; logos to choose from.**

### Desktop, Android and the Mac
- "It worked in the old version; since the update it is slow." We measured the engines of 2.6.50 to 2.6.74 on a network that drops blocked handshakes without a word (Türk Telekom, Turkcell). One connection had time for four techniques. Before Tor, the next visits carried on down the list until one opened the site; since 2.6.54 the first visit that ran out of time handed the site to Tor, and nothing looked further, so sites that a later technique opens lived on slow Tor. Now the rest of the list goes out at once after two unanswered attempts: every technique on the first visit, in about the same time.
- Tor takes a site only when every technique failed, when no address of it answers, or when you chose it. A site on Tor is looked at again behind it and goes back to its own way as soon as that works, instead of staying on Tor for a quarter of an hour.
- Tor is no longer asked for or started because the network went away for a moment (a name must stay out of reach for ten seconds first), for Shroudly's own encrypted DNS, or (desktop) while another bypass tool such as GoodbyeDPI is running.
- A site's other names, while Tor carries one of them, get every technique too, quickly, instead of six seconds and then Tor (Roblox froze and cut out on Türk Telekom this way).
- A request nobody answered counts for half of a real cut on the way to Tor.

### Desktop, Android and the Apple apps
- http:// sites that the network drops without a word (Türk Telekom) opened neither directly nor through Tor, and nothing was said. Shroudly now tells a dropped request from a slow server (the request was never acknowledged) and tries its techniques, then Tor where it may.

### Android, iPhone and iPad

### Desktop
- Games and apps mode: programs built on older versions of axios (the TruckersMP launcher: "Request failed with status code 405") send a whole https:// address instead of asking for a tunnel; Shroudly now makes the request for them, with the certificate checked.

releases.title: Shroudly v2.6.74
releases.notes:
## Shroudly 2.6.74

**Faster again where Tor took a site once; Tor that works in Russia (it waits for slow bridges, and it can be fetched there); Gemini and AI Studio through Tor.**

### Desktop, Android and the Mac
- "Since the Tor feature it always uses Tor, and it is very slow." A name Tor carried was kept on Tor for 30 minutes, and every connection Tor carried started the 30 minutes again, so a site that fell to Tor once (a moment the network failed, a wake from sleep) stayed on Tor as long as it was used and never tried the usual ways again. Now it stays there 15 minutes from the first time, then the techniques are tried again; only if they still fail does it go back to Tor.
- Tor through bridges (Russia: webtunnel, meek) can take longer than 15 seconds to reach a site; the engine gave up at 15, every time, so Telegram never went through it even with Tor ready ("does not speak the protocol chosen", 0 connections carried). It now waits 45 seconds for Tor, and says "did not reach the site in time" when that is what happened.
- Gemini and AI Studio in "Apps always through Tor": their pages and the APIs the prompts go to, together. Sending some Google names through Tor by hand and not others (an Iran report) opened AI Studio but nothing could be written.

### Desktop
- Tor is fetched the first time it is needed from torproject.org, which Russia cuts: Tor was never fetched there, and the log said "ENOENT bundle.tar.gz" instead of why. The same files are now also on Shroudly's GitHub (release `tor-16.0`), tried next, and checked against the same SHA-256 as the Tor Project's, so only their file is ever used; a cut connection is said as such.

### Desktop, Android and the Apple apps
- A "Share my connection" link made where no way in from the internet opened (no port forwarding on the router, or a provider that shares one address among its customers) carries a home network's address (192.168.x.x), which only that network reaches. Sent to a friend in another country (Vietnam and Turkey), "Your own server" said "nothing came back; the password or the method may be wrong", or "does not speak the protocol chosen" when the same address was another device on their network. It now says the real reason: the address belongs to a home or office network, so the link works only there, and from elsewhere the router of the person sharing must forward its port to the internet.

releases.title: Shroudly v2.6.73
releases.notes:
## Shroudly 2.6.73

**Apps always through Tor: pick an app such as Instagram or Telegram and all of it goes through Tor. An app whose servers the network blocks goes through Tor too, and the Tor question names it.**

### Desktop, Android, Android TV and the Mac
- **Apps always through Tor** (Connections by site). A user in Iran asked for Instagram always through Tor. Until now only a site could be sent through Tor, one name at a time; an app uses many (Instagram: instagram.com, cdninstagram.com, fbcdn.net and more) and, like Telegram, may connect to its servers by address. Now twelve apps can be picked as a whole: Instagram, Telegram, WhatsApp, YouTube, X, Facebook, Discord, Signal, Reddit, TikTok, Spotify and ChatGPT. A picked app's names go through Tor, and for Telegram its address ranges too (the engine now takes `TOR <address>/<bits>`), blocked or not. Picking one is the consent to Tor, as sending a site through it is. A name two apps share (fbcdn.net: Instagram's and Facebook's pictures) goes back the usual way only once neither is picked. Shown wherever this copy has Tor: not in the lite APK, on iPhone or on Apple TV.
- A site or app sent through Tor that was opened while Tor was still starting kept its connection made the usual way (a browser keeps one for minutes), so it did not go through Tor until much later. Now, the moment Tor is ready, those connections end once and the app connects again through Tor. Checked on Android: www.instagram.com went the usual way before, and through Tor after.
- When the list sent through Tor is given anew (as the Mac app does at every change), what left it is no longer kept through Tor.

### Desktop and Android
- An app that connects to its servers by address (Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal and others) can find those addresses blocked outright, as Telegram's are in Iran. Tor already carried such connections once allowed, but Shroudly said the opposite: a notice to use "the app's own proxy setting or a VPN", which a user there cannot do. Now, where this copy has Tor: allowed, the app's connections simply go through it; not allowed yet, Shroudly asks, naming the app; turned off, it asks again now and then, as it does for sites. The old notice is left only where there is no Tor (the lite APK) or your own server is set.

### Desktop, Android and the Mac
- The Tor question named whatever needed Tor first, often a bare address ("Open 2001:4188:…:35 through Tor?"), and kept that even when Telegram came next, so nobody knew what they were being asked about. Now it names the app when the address is a known one (Telegram for 149.154.167.92 or t.me), keeps a site's name over a later address, and puts the better name in the notification at once.

### How it looks (every screen checked on Apple TV, iPhone, Android and the desktop)
- Apple TV: the notice before the first start was a small box with its text cut off and Continue out of sight; it now fills the screen, readable from the couch, with Continue in focus.
- Apple TV: Settings, Follow and About ran their rows behind the tabs along the top when scrolled; the list now ends below them. About's last paragraph (Conduit) could not be reached with the remote; now it can. "Something not working?" is laid out like the other pages instead of stretched across the TV.
- Apple TV: the start button was read out by VoiceOver as "MarkClosed" (a picture's file name); it now says Start protection or Stop protection.
- Apple TV and iPhone: What's new showed a note about the Mac; the Mac now has its own notes.
- Android: the buttons on Connections by site (Through Tor, Block) and the report's Send were the system's grey slabs in capitals; they now have the app's look, and Send is faded until it can be pressed.
- Android TV and tablets: Connections by site and the report ran from edge to edge, the words on the left and the switches far off on the right; they now sit in the middle, as wide as the other pages.
- Mac: What's new no longer starts with "On the Mac:".
- iPad: Settings, About and the report ran from edge to edge beside Stats and Follow, which did not; they now sit in the middle, as wide as those.

releases.title: Shroudly v2.6.72
releases.notes:
## Shroudly 2.6.72

**Reports get through where the report server is slowed (Russia).**

### Desktop, Android and Android TV
- Russia's networks freeze connections to Cloudflare's addresses, where the report server is, after about 16 KB, and a report with its log is more than that. A report was sent through Tor only when Tor happened to be running already; with Tor off, "Something not working?" could not send anything there. Now the report goes through Tor: if Tor is not running, the app starts it just for the report (whether or not you said yes to Tor for sites), waits for it (up to two and a half minutes), sends the whole report through it, and stops it again where you had not said yes. Not where Tor is turned off in Settings.

releases.notes:
## Shroudly 2.6.71

**Windows 7 and 8: Start and Stop work again, and Advanced mode says what is really in its way.**

### Windows 7, 8 and 8.1
- Since 2.6.34, every Start and Stop on Windows 7 and 8 ended with "Start failed: app.setProxy is not a function": the Windows 7 and 8 build runs an older Electron, which does not have that function. Fixed, and a test now keeps such newer functions out of the code those systems run.
- On Windows 7, Advanced mode said that security software blocked its driver (error 577). It was not an antivirus: Windows 7 cannot check the driver's SHA-2 signature without Microsoft's update KB4474419. The app now says that, with the update to install, and does not ask for administrator permission again and again in the same session.
- Tor's bridges for your country are now fetched on Windows 7 and 8 too.

### Every app
- After an update, the "What's new" window inside the app showed 2.6.64's notes under every newer number (2.6.65 to 2.6.70). The notes are written for this version now, a test keeps them that way, and notes already shown are never shown again.

### Windows
- The 32-bit Shroudly on a 64-bit Windows said that Advanced mode is "not available on this processor". It now says that the 64-bit Shroudly has it, to install over this one (settings stay).
